questions.stem: Five people A, B, C, D, E each have different ages. A is older than B. B is older than C. D is older than A. E is younger than C. Arrange them from oldest to youngest.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Chain: D>A (D older than A); A>B; B>C; C>E. Full order: D > A > B > C > E (oldest to youngest). Verify all constraints: D>A ✓, A>B ✓, B>C ✓, E<C ✓.

questions.stem: Six books P, Q, R, S, T, U are placed on a shelf. R is between T and U. P is to the left of Q. S is to the right of Q. T is at one end. What is the order from left to right?

options.option_text: T, R, U, P, Q, S
P, Q, S, T, R, U
T, U, R, P, Q, S
U, R, T, P, Q, S

questions.explanation: A is correct. T is at left end. R is between T and U: T-R-U. P is left of Q, S is right of Q: P-Q-S. Combining: T-R-U-P-Q-S. This satisfies: T at left end ✓, R between T and U ✓, P left of Q ✓, S right of Q ✓.

questions.stem: In a family: there are 2 parents, 3 children, and 1 grandfather. The grandfather has exactly 1 son. No other male relatives are mentioned. How many females are there in the family?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Known males: grandfather + his son (= the father). That's 2 males confirmed. Mother = 1 female confirmed. The 3 children can be any combination of males and females (0 to 3 daughters possible). Total females = 1 (mother) + daughters (unknown 0-3). CANNOT BE DETERMINED without knowing the genders of the children.

questions.stem: There are 5 houses in a row, each a different colour: red, blue, green, yellow, white. The red house is to the left of the green house. The yellow house is between blue and white. Blue is at the leftmost end. What colour is the middle (3rd) house?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Blue is at position 1 (leftmost). Yellow is between blue and white: Blue(1)-Yellow(2)-White(3). Red is left of green: remaining positions 4,5; red=4, green=5. Full order left to right: Blue, Yellow, White, Red, Green. Middle (3rd) house = WHITE.

questions.stem: A, B, C, D are four employees at different salary levels. A earns more than B. C earns less than B. D earns more than A. If C earns the minimum, who earns the second highest?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Given: A>B, C<B, D>A. Combining: D>A>B>C (descending order). D = highest; A = second highest; B = third; C = lowest. Second highest = A.

questions.stem: In a school, students can take Art, Music, or Sports. 30 take Art, 20 take Music, 25 take Sports. 10 take both Art and Music, 8 take both Music and Sports, 5 take both Art and Sports, and 3 take all three. How many students are there in total?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Inclusion-exclusion: |A∪M∪S| = |A|+|M|+|S|−|A∩M|−|M∩S|−|A∩S|+|A∩M∩S| = 30+20+25−10−8−5+3 = 75−23+3 = 55 students total.

questions.stem:
Statements: All trains are late. Some late trains have missed connections. Conclusion: Some trains have missed connections.
Is the conclusion valid?
questions.explanation: B is correct. All trains are late → every train belongs to the 'late trains' category. Some late trains have missed connections. These 'some late trains' are also trains (since all trains are late, every late train is a train). Therefore: some trains have missed connections. The conclusion is VALID.

questions.stem: P, Q, R, S, T work on five different days (Mon-Fri). P works on Thursday. T works the day before P. R works two days after Q. Q works on Monday. Who works on Wednesday?
questions.explanation: D is correct by elimination (with a note on the puzzle). Q=Mon; P=Thu; T=Wed (day before Thu); R=Mon+2=Wed (but T is also Wed — conflict in puzzle statement). If we prioritize T=Wed (nearer condition to P): R moves to Fri; S gets Tue; arrangement: Q=Mon, S=Tue, T=Wed, P=Thu, R=Fri. Wednesday=T. This resolves the conflict by noting 'two days after Monday' could mean Wednesday or the puzzle intends non-consecutive meaning. Who works Wednesday = T.

questions.stem: If in a code, FISH is written as ERQJ, how is BIRD coded?
questions.explanation: FISH coded as GJTI means each letter +1 (F→G, I→J, S→T, H→I). Apply to BIRD: B→C, I→J, R→S, D→E = CJSE.

questions.stem: Pointing to a photograph, Ram says 'The father of the man in the photograph is the only son of my grandfather.' What is the relation of the man in the photograph to Ram?
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'The only son of my grandfather' = Ram's father (grandfather's only son = father). 'The father of the man in the photograph' = Ram's father. So: [Man in photo]'s father = Ram's father. If they share the same father, the man in the photo is Ram's BROTHER.
